claim: Phospholipids generally contain a saturated fatty acid (FA) at position sn1 whereas the sn2-FA is saturated, monounsaturated or polyunsaturated.
source: Phospholipids generally contain a saturated fatty acid (FA) at position sn1 whereas the sn2-FA is saturated, monounsaturated or polyunsaturated.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about phospholipid structure, supported by citations in the manuscript.

claim: Phospholipids with two polyunsaturated FAs make membranes prone to vesiculation but highly permeable.
source: phospholipids with two polyunsaturated FAs make membranes prone to vesiculation but highly permeable
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GTPase assays, electron microscopy, and permeability measurements presented in the manuscript.

claim: Asymmetric sn1-saturated-sn2-polyunsaturated phospholipids provide a tradeoff between efficient membrane vesiculation and low membrane permeability.
source: asymmetric sn1-saturated-sn2-polyunsaturated phospholipids provide a tradeoff between efficient membrane vesiculation and low membrane permeability
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing symmetric and asymmetric phospholipids in vesiculation and permeability assays.

claim: When incorporated into phospholipids, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; omega-3) makes membranes more deformable than arachidonic acid (omega-6).
source: When incorporated into phospholipids, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA; omega-3) makes membranes more deformable than arachidonic acid (omega-6).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase activity measurements, electron microscopy observations, and molecular dynamics simulations comparing 18:0-22:6 and 18:0-20:4 phospholipids.

claim: PUFAs act through three different states: as free molecules, as precursors of biological mediators, or as esters in membrane phospholipids.
source: PUFAs act through three different states: as free molecules, as precursors of biological mediators, or as esters in membrane phospholipids.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about PUFA function in biological systems.

claim: Acyl transferases selectively incorporate defined fatty acids into phospholipids.
source: The third form results from the activity of acyl transferases, which selectively incorporate defined fatty acids into phospholipids (Harayama et al., 2014; Shindou et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The acyl chain profile of phospholipids varies tremendously among organisms, tissues and cells, and even among organelles.
source: This allows cells to control the acyl chain profile of their phospholipids, which varies tremendously among organisms, tissues and cells, and even among organelles (Harayama et al., 2014; Hulbert, 2003; Shindou et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The FA diversity in phospholipids applies mostly to the sn2 position of the glycerol backbone, resulting in asymmetric phospholipids containing a saturated FA at position sn1 and an unsaturated FA at position sn2.
source: Interestingly, the FA diversity in phospholipids applies mostly to the sn2 position of the glycerol backbone, hence resulting in asymmetric phospholipids containing a saturated FA at position sn1 and an unsaturated FA at position sn2 (Hanahan et al., 1960; Lands and Merkl, 1963; Tattrie, 1959; Yabuuchi and O'Brien, 1968).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The brain is enriched in phospholipids with PUFAs, notably in the case of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and phosphatidylserine (PS).
source: For example, the brain is enriched in phospholipids with PUFAs, notably in the case of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE) and phosphatidylserine (PS) (Tam and Innis, 2006; Yabuuchi and O'Brien, 1968).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The axon tip is enriched in phosphatidylcholine (PC) molecules containing arachidonate (AA or 20:4 omega-6) or docosahexaenoate (DHA or 22:6 omega-3) at the expense of less unsaturated PC species.
source: Moreover, an interesting pattern has been detected in neurons, where the axon tip is enriched in phosphatidylcholine (PC) molecules containing arachidonate (AA or 20:4 omega-6) or docosahexaenoate (DHA or 22:6 omega-3) at the expense of less unsaturated PC species (Yang et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Phospholipids with PUFAs account for up to 70 mol% of the phospholipid pool in synaptic vesicles.
source: Thus, phospholipids with PUFAs are found at very high concentration in synaptic vesicles, where they account for up to 70 mol% of the phospholipid pool (Takamori et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Retinal discs show very high concentrations of phospholipids containing PUFAs.
source: Retinal discs also show very high concentrations of phospholipids containing PUFAs (Boesze-Battaglia and Schimmel, 1997; Rice et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Phospholipids with the sn2 PUFA DHA facilitate the membrane shaping and fission activities of dynamin and endophilin.
source: We previously showed that phospholipids with the sn2 PUFA DHA facilitate the membrane shaping and fission activities of dynamin and endophilin (Pinot et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: Dynamin and endophilin are involved in the formation of endocytic vesicles by assembling into spirals around the neck of membrane buds.
source: These proteins are involved in the formation of endocytic vesicles by assembling into spirals around the neck of membrane buds (Antonny et al., 2016; Boucrot et al., 2015; Farsad et al., 2001; Slepnev and De Camilli, 2000; Sundborger et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: DHA-containing phospholipids decrease membrane-bending rigidity by adapting their conformation to membrane curvature.
source: Physical manipulations, molecular dynamics simulations and biochemical measurements revealed that DHA-containing phospholipids decrease membrane-bending rigidity by adapting their conformation to membrane curvature, hence providing an advantage for membrane deformation and fission by the dynamin endophilin complex (Pinot et al., 2014)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: More rigid membranes are less prone to fission.
source: in contrast to more rigid membranes, which are less prone to fission (Morlot et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The flexibility of polyunsaturated phospholipids along the membrane normal (z direction) might soften various mechanical stresses in the membrane.
source: More generally, the flexibility of polyunsaturated phospholipids along the membrane normal (z direction) might soften various mechanical stresses in the membrane (Barelli and Antonny, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research by the authors.

claim: The rate of GTP hydrolysis by dynamin varied up to 300-fold depending on the acyl chain content of the lipid membrane.
source: Despite the identical composition of all liposomes in term of lipid polar head groups, the rate of GTP hydrolysis by dynamin varied up to 300-fold indicating that dynamin is very sensitive to the acyl chain content of the lipid membrane on which it acts.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GTPase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The GTPase activity of dynamin increased dramatically (x 20) on membranes made of symmetric diunsaturated phospholipids compared to asymmetric saturated-unsaturated phospholipids.
source: First, the GTPase activity of dynamin increased dramatically (x 20) on membranes made of symmetric diunsaturated phospholipids compared to asymmetric saturated-unsaturated phospholipids.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GTPase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The GTPase activity of dynamin increased with the unsaturated level of phospholipids (18:1 < 18:2 < 20:4 < 22:6).
source: Second, the GTPase activity of dynamin increased with the unsaturated level of phospholipids (18:1 < 18:2 < 20:4 < 22:6), a trend that was observed in both symmetric and asymmetric phospholipid series.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GTPase assays shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Dynamin alone extensively deformed 22:6-22:6 liposomes, whereas 18:0-22:6 liposomes were largely unaffected.
source: By negative staining electron microscopy, we observed that dynamin alone extensively deformed 22:6-22:6 liposomes, whereas 18:0-22:6 liposomes were largely unaffected (Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Membranes made of 18:2-18:2-PC or 18:3-18:3 PC showed a two to three fold higher water permeability than membranes made of 18:0-18:1-PC or 18:0-18:2-PC.
source: Because a previous study reported that membranes made of 18:2-18:2-PC or 18:3-18:3 PC showed a two to three fold higher water permeability than membranes made of 18:0-18:1-PC or 18:0-18:2-PC (Olbrich et al., 2000)
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: In saturated (14:0-14:0) membranes, only few water movements were detected.
source: In saturated (14:0-14:0) membranes, only few water movements were detected.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In membranes made of phospholipids with one unsaturated FA, the number of moving water molecules increased up to 10-fold with the level of acyl chain unsaturation (18:1 < 18:2 < 20:4 < 22:6).
source: In membranes made of phospholipids with one unsaturated FA, the number of moving water molecules increased up to 10-fold with the level of acyl chain unsaturation (18:1 < 18:2 < 20:4 < 22:6) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Membranes with phospholipids containing two unsaturated FA showed a further 2 to 3-fold increase in the number of moving water molecules as compared to membranes with asymmetric saturated-unsaturated phospholipids.
source: Importantly, membranes with phospholipids containing two unsaturated FA showed a further 2 to 3-fold increase in the number of moving water molecules as compared to membranes with asymmetric saturated-unsaturated phospholipids.
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Replacing asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids with dipolyunsaturated phospholipids caused a much larger red shift in PA fluorescence emission.
source: However, replacing asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids with dipolyunsaturated phospholipids caused a much larger red shift (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1; e.g. 18:0-22:6 << 22:6-22:6), suggesting that duplication of the PUFA in phospholipids dramatically increased membrane hydration.
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence spectroscopy data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Liposomes with symmetric polyunsaturated phospholipids showed a > 10 fold higher permeability to dithionite than asymmetric phospholipids.
source: Figure 2C shows that membrane permeability to dithionite modestly increased with the level of polyunsaturation in asymmetric phospholipids (18:0-18:1 < 18:0-18:2 < 18:0-20:4 < 18:0-22:6) and that liposomes with symmetric polyunsaturated phospholipids showed a > 10 fold higher permeability.
evidence: This claim is supported by NBD quenching assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: GUVs containing 55 mol% 22:6-22:6 phospholipids were about 10 times more permeable to Alexa A488 maleimide than GUVs containing 55 mol% 18:0-22:6 phospholipids.
source: GUVs containing 55 mol% 22:6-22:6 phospholipids were about 10 times more permeable to Alexa A488 maleimide than GUVs containing 55 mol% 18:0-22:6 phospholipids.
evidence: This claim is supported by GUV permeability measurements shown in Figure 2D.

claim: There is a remarkable correlation between the ability of dynamin alone to readily vesiculate membranes and the permeability of these membranes to water and even to large or charged solutes.
source: Altogether, these experiments revealed a remarkable correlation between the ability of dynamin alone to readily vesiculate membranes and the permeability of these membranes to water and even to large or charged solutes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of vesiculation and permeability experiments.

claim: The intrinsic GTPase activity of dynamin on asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipid liposomes increased about 10 times in the presence of endophilin-A1.
source: Even though the intrinsic GTPase activity of dynamin on such liposomes was low, it increased about 10 times in the presence endophilin-A1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Endophilin works in close partnership with dynamin both through protein/protein interactions and through the ability of the two proteins to form membrane-deforming spirals.
source: In cells, endophilin works in close partnership with dynamin both through protein/protein interactions and through the ability of the two proteins to form membrane-deforming spirals (Boucrot et al., 2015; Farsad et al., 2001; Sundborger et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The BAR domain of endophilin is followed by an SH3 domain, which interacts with the proline-rich region of dynamin leading to cooperative BAR/dynamin membrane recruitment.
source: The BAR domain of endophilin is followed by an SH3 domain, which interacts with the proline-rich region of dynamin leading to cooperative BAR/dynamin membrane recruitment (Farsad et al., 2001; Meinecke et al., 2013; Sundborger et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Membrane deformation by BAR domains facilitates dynamin self-assembly.
source: In addition, membrane deformation by BAR domains facilitates dynamin self-assembly, which by itself is a relatively weak membrane deforming protein and which preferentially self-assembles on pre-curved membranes (Neumann and Schmid, 2013; Roux et al., 2010)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The effect of 18:0-22:6 phospholipids on dynamin GTPase activity surpassed by 2 to 4-fold that observed with the less complex asymmetric polyunsaturated phospholipids (18:0-18:2, 18:0-18:3 and 18:0-20:4).
source: However, the effect of 18:0-22:6 phospholipids surpassed by 2 to 4-fold that observed with the less complex asymmetric polyunsaturated phospholipids (18:0-18:2, 18:0-18:3 and 18:0-20:4) (Figure 3).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase assay data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Dynamin GTPase activity plateaus at about 60 mol% of 18:0-22:6 phospholipids, close to the amount of polyunsaturated lipids in synaptic vesicles.
source: Dynamin GTPase activity plateau at about 60 mol% of 18:0-22:6 phospholipids, close to the amount of polyunsaturated lipids in synaptic vesicles (Takamori et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase assay data shown in Figure 3 and a citation to previous research.

claim: The activity of dynamin was almost maximal with 18:0-22:6 phospholipids even in the absence of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Strikingly, the activity of dynamin was almost maximal with 18:0-22:6 phospholipids even in the absence of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SNX9 was more efficient than endophilin for assisting dynamin activity.
source: In addition, SNX9 was more efficient than endophilin for assisting dynamin activity in agreement with a previous study (Neumann and Schmid, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by GTPase assay data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and a citation to previous research.

claim: All asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids favor dynamin GTPase activity, notably under conditions close to physiological conditions.
source: First, all asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids favor dynamin GTPase activity, notably under conditions close to physiological conditions (low concentration of PI(4,5)P2, low protein concentration, cooperation with BAR-domain proteins).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of GTPase assays under various conditions.

claim: Docosahexaenoic acid (22:6), which is the most polyunsaturated species of the omega-3 family, surpasses all other tested species including arachidonate (20:4), the most polyunsaturated species of the omega-6 family.
source: Second, docosahexaenoic acid (22:6), which is the most polyunsaturated species of the omega-3 family, surpasses all other tested species including arachidonate (20:4), the most polyunsaturated species of the omega-6 family.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of GTPase assays comparing different polyunsaturated fatty acids.

claim: Both 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 liposomes but not 18:0-18:1 liposomes, became extensively deformed after incubation with dynamin, endophilin and GTPγS or GTP.
source: By transmission electron microscopy (TEM) we observed that both 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 liposomes but not 18:0-18:1 liposomes, became extensively deformed after incubation with dynamin, endophilin and GTPγS or GTP.
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The tubes formed from 18:0-22:6 membranes were significantly thinner than the tubes formed from 18:0-20:4 membranes.
source: However, the tubes formed from 18:0-22:6 membranes were significantly thinner than the tubes formed from 18:0-20:4 membranes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy measurements shown in Figure 4B.

claim: With 18:0-20:4 phospholipids, there was a remaining peak of large membrane profiles (R > 50 nm), which coexisted with a peak of small vesicles (R < 50 nm).
source: With 18:0-20:4 phospholipids, there was a remaining peak of large membrane profiles (R > 50 nm), which coexisted with a peak of small vesicles (R < 50 nm).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy size distribution analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: With 18:0-22:6 phospholipids, the liposomes were almost fully transformed into small vesicles.
source: With 18:0-22:6 phospholipids, the liposomes were almost fully transformed into small vesicles.
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy size distribution analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The vesicles formed from 18:0-22:6 membranes were slightly smaller than that formed from 18:0-20:4 membranes.
source: In addition, the vesicles formed from 18:0-22:6 membranes were slightly smaller than that formed from 18:0-20:4 membranes (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by electron microscopy size distribution analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Dynamin, endophilin and GTP caused GUV consumption over time for both 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes but not for the control GUVs that contained only 18:0-18:1 phospholipids.
source: Dynamin, endophilin and GTP caused GUV consumption over time for both 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes (Figure 5A) but not for the control GUVs that contained only 18:0-18:1 phospholipids (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GUV shrinking assay data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: After 1 hr of incubation, the difference between 18:0-20:4 and 18:0 22:6 phospholipids was significant, as a larger population of shrunk 18:0-22:6 GUVs and a higher amount of intact 18:0-20:4 GUVs were detected.
source: After 1 hr of incubation, the difference between 18:0-20:4 and 18:0 22:6 phospholipids was significant, as we detected a larger population of shrunk 18:0-22:6 GUVs and a higher amount of intact 18:0-20:4 GUVs (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by GUV shrinking assay data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: The difference in GUV shrinking between 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 phospholipids was already evident after 15 min and increased over time.
source: The difference in GUV shrinking between 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 phospholipids was already evident after 15 min and increased over time (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is supported by GUV shrinking assay data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Increasing the degree of phospholipid polyunsaturation (18:0-18:1 < 18:0-18:2 < 18:0-20:4 < 18:0-22:6) accelerated the linear phase of tube formation and resulted in the formation of longer and thinner tubes.
source: Increasing the degree of phospholipid polyunsaturation (18:0-18:1 < 18:0-18:2 < 18:0-20:4 < 18:0-22:6) accelerated the linear phase and resulted in the formation of longer and thinner tubes (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: 18:0-18:2, 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes had relative values of Κb equal to 50%, 35% and 30% of Κb for 18:0-18:1 membranes, respectively.
source: Considering that these tubes should have stored the same curvature energy, these changes in L/R suggested inverse changes in membrane bending rigidity: 18:0-18:2, 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes had relative values of Κb equal to 50%, 35% and 30% of Κb for 18:0-18:1 membranes, respectively.
evidence: This claim is inferred from coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Fission events were observed for some tubes formed from 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes but not from 18:0-18:1 or 18:0-18:2 membranes during 200 ns simulations.
source: During the time of the simulations (200 ns), we observed fission events for some tubes formed from 18:0-20:4 and 18:0-22:6 membranes but not from 18:0-18:1 or 18:0-18:2 membranes (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A and Video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The force threshold at which fission occurred was lower for 18:0-22:6 membranes than for 18:0-20:4 membranes.
source: Although the number of simulations did not allow us to establish robust statistics, we noticed that the force threshold at which fission occurred was lower for 18:0-22:6 membranes than for 18:0-20:4 membranes (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Fission occurred sooner for 18:0-22:6 tubes as compared to 18:0-20:4 tubes.
source: Moreover, fission occurred sooner for 18:0-22:6 tubes as compared to 18:0-20:4 tubes.
evidence: This claim is supported by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Whatever the parameter considered (z velocity, FA torsions, protrusions, packing defects), the calculated value always increased with the polyunsaturation level of the sn2 chain, with 22:6 clearly surpassing all other polyunsaturated FAs.
source: Figure 6C–E and Figure 6—figure supplement 2 show that whatever the parameter considered, the calculated value always increased with the polyunsaturation level of the sn2 chain, with 22:6 clearly surpassing all other polyunsaturated FAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6C–E and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The behavior of the sn1 18:0 chain was relatively constant and appeared poorly dependent on the nature of the neighboring sn2 chain.
source: In contrast, the behavior of the sn1 18:0 chain was relatively constant and appeared poorly dependent on the nature of the neighboring sn2 chain.
evidence: This claim is supported by all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6C–E.

claim: The main effect of having an sn2 polyunsaturated chain in phospholipids is to increase the probability of fast movements along the z-axis.
source: Altogether, these various analyses show that the main effect of having an sn2 polyunsaturated chain in phospholipids is to increase the probability of fast movements of along the z-axis.
evidence: This claim is inferred from all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Acyl chain swapping modified the mean position of the saturated and polyunsaturated acyl chains across the bilayer.
source: However, measurements of the acyl chain density across the bilayer indicated that acyl chain swapping modified the mean position of the saturated and polyunsaturated acyl chains across the bilayer (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The relative esterification position of the saturated and polyunsaturated FAs in natural lipids facilitates compensatory z movements where the polyunsaturated FA explores the interfacial region while the saturated FA explores the bilayer center.
source: Thus, the relative esterification position of the saturated and polyunsaturated FAs in natural lipids facilitates compensatory z movements where the polyunsaturated FA explores the interfacial region while the saturated FA explores the bilayer center.
evidence: This claim is inferred from all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data comparing natural and swapped phospholipids.

claim: Acyl chain swapping did not significantly modify membrane fission in coarse-grained simulations.
source: In addition, acyl chain swapping did not significantly modify membrane fission (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C and Video 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3C.

claim: Polyunsaturated phospholipids considerably modify the properties of membranes.
source: A few studies have established that polyunsaturated phospholipids considerably modify the properties of membranes (Armstrong et al., 2003; Eldho et al., 2003; Garcia-Manyes et al., 2010; Huang, 2001; Olbrich et al., 2000; Rawicz et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A high dithionite permeability of membranes containing 18:3-18:3 phospholipids has been reported for LUVs.
source: For LUVs, a high dithionite permeability of membranes containing 18:3-18:3 phospholipids has been reported (Armstrong et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: For GUVs, micropipette manipulations indicate that the presence of at least one polyunsaturated acyl chain results in a drop of the membrane bending modulus whereas the presence of two polyunsaturated acyl chains causes a jump in water permeability.
source: For GUVs, micropipette manipulations indicate that the presence of at least one polyunsaturated acyl chain results in a drop of the membrane bending modulus whereas the presence of two polyunsaturated acyl chains causes a jump in water permeability (Olbrich et al., 2000; Rawicz et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Membranes with asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids such as 18:0-20:4 or 18:0-22:6 phospholipids are much less leaky than membranes with symmetrical 20:4-20:4 or 22:6-22:6 phospholipids but can still be readily vesiculated by dynamin provided that BAR-domain proteins are present.
source: Membranes with asymmetric saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids such as 18:0-20:4 or 18:0-22:6 phospholipids are much less leaky than membranes with symmetrical 20:4-20:4 or 22:6-22:6 phospholipids but can still be readily vesiculated by dynamin provided that BAR-domain proteins are present.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of vesiculation and permeability experiments.

claim: The fact that membranes with 18:0-22:6 phospholipids are systematically more permissive to the mechanical activity of dynamin and endophilin than membranes with 18:0-20:4 phospholipids is of interest given the importance of the omega-6/omega-3 ratio for health and notably for brain function.
source: Furthermore, the fact that membranes with 18:0-22:6 phospholipids are systematically more permissive to the mechanical activity of dynamin and endophilin than membranes with 18:0-20:4 phospholipids is of interest given the importance of the omega-6/omega-3 ratio for health and notably for brain function.
evidence: This claim combines experimental data with speculation about biological significance.

claim: The distinctive chemical feature of polyunsaturated acyl chains is the presence of saturated carbons (CH2) sandwiched between two unsaturated ones (=CH-CH2-CH=).
source: The distinctive chemical feature of polyunsaturated acyl chains is the presence of saturated carbons (CH2) sandwiched between two unsaturated ones (=CH-CH2-CH=).
evidence: This is a statement of established chemical knowledge.

claim: Rotational freedom around CH2 groups sandwiched between unsaturated carbons is exceptionally high as compared to rotation around the CH2 groups of monounsaturated or saturated acyl chains.
source: Rotational freedom around these CH2 groups is exceptionally high as compared to rotation around the CH2 groups of monounsaturated or saturated acyl chains (Feller et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Motions of the acyl chain along the normal of the membrane (z movements) increase in speed and in amplitude with the level acyl chain polyunsaturation (18:2 < 18:3 < 20:4 < 22:6).
source: Our MD simulations indicate that motions of the acyl chain along the normal of the membrane (z movements) increase in speed and in amplitude with the level acyl chain polyunsaturation (18:2 < 18:3 < 20:4 < 22:6).
evidence: This claim is supported by molecular dynamics simulation data.

claim: Such movements should allow phospholipids to readily adapt their conformation to membrane curvature, hence explaining the gradual decrease in membrane bending rigidity.
source: Such movements should allow phospholipids to readily adapt their conformation to membrane curvature (Barelli and Antonny, 2016; Pinot et al., 2014), hence explaining the gradual decrease in membrane bending rigidity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from simulation data and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The presence of a neighboring saturated acyl chain should secure lipid packing and prevents the passage of small molecules.
source: Concurrently, the presence of a neighboring saturated acyl chain should secure lipid packing and prevents the passage of small molecules.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of permeability experiments and simulations.

claim: Plasmalogens, which form a large subclass of PE in the brain, harbor a sn1 saturated acyl chain that is bound to the glycerol through an ether-vinyl bond.
source: Plasmalogens, which form a large subclass of PE in the brain, harbor a sn1 saturated acyl chain that is bound to the glycerol through an ether-vinyl bond.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about plasmalogen structure.

claim: Ether-vinyl phospholipids considerably decrease the permeability of model membranes to ions because these lipids pack more tightly than their ester counterparts.
source: Interestingly, ether-vinyl phospholipids considerably decrease the permeability of model membranes to ions because these lipids pack more tightly than their ester counterparts (Zeng et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Single chain amphiphilic molecules (e.g. fatty acids), the most plausible building blocks for primitive membranes, can self-assemble into bilayers, which spontaneously vesiculate.
source: Single chain amphiphilic molecules (e.g. fatty acids), the most plausible building blocks for primitive membranes, can self-assemble into bilayers, which spontaneously vesiculate (Bruckner et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Bilayers made of single chain amphiphilic molecules are very leaky to even large solutes (in the 103 Da range).
source: However, these bilayers are very leaky to even large solutes (in the 103 Da range).
evidence: This claim is supported by the context of the cited research on primitive membranes.

claim: The shift from single chain to dual chain lipids has probably allowed primitive cells to reduce the general permeability of their membrane, thereby imposing an evolutionary pressure for the emergence of specialized transporters.
source: Later, the shift from single chain to dual chain lipids has probably allowed primitive cells to reduce the general permeability of their membrane, thereby imposing an evolutionary pressure for the emergence of specialized transporters (Budin and Szostak, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research and involves speculation about evolutionary processes.

claim: Phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsaturated acyl chain are absent in many eukaryotes (e.g. yeast) but abundant in some highly differentiated cells (e.g. neurons, photoreceptors, sperm).
source: The experiments presented here suggest that phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsaturated acyl chain, which are absent in many eukaryotes (e.g. yeast) but abundant in some highly differentiated cells (e.g. neurons, photoreceptors, sperm) provide a solution to an early dilemma in evolution: finding the right balance between efficient membrane vesiculation without loss in membrane permeability.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about lipid distribution in different organisms and cell types.

claim: Phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsaturated acyl chain provide a solution to finding the right balance between efficient membrane vesiculation without loss in membrane permeability.
source: The experiments presented here suggest that phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsaturated acyl chain, which are absent in many eukaryotes (e.g. yeast) but abundant in some highly differentiated cells (e.g. neurons, photoreceptors, sperm) provide a solution to an early dilemma in evolution: finding the right balance between efficient membrane vesiculation without loss in membrane permeability.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the combined results of all experiments in the manuscript.

claim: Saturated-DHA (omega-3) phospholipids are systematically better for membrane vesiculation than many other saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids, including saturated-arachidonate (omega-6).
source: Moreover, the fact that saturated-DHA (omega-3) phospholipids are systematically better for membrane vesiculation than many other saturated-polyunsaturated phospholipids, including saturated-arachidonate (omega-6), is informative considering the importance of the omega-6/omega-3 ratio for health.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from GTPase assays, electron microscopy, and GUV shrinking experiments.

claim: GTP hydrolysis in the dynamin spiral occurs by a mutual nucleophilic attack between dynamin molecules from adjacent rungs.
source: GTP hydrolysis in the dynamin spiral occurs by a mutual nucleophilic attack between dynamin molecules from adjacent rungs (Chappie et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The rate of GTP hydrolysis depends on dynamin self-assembly and increases from negligible values in solution where dynamin is not polymerized, to rates in the range of 2 to 5 s-1 on optimal membrane templates where dynamin forms spirals.
source: Consequently, the rate of GTP hydrolysis depends on dynamin self-assembly and, in effect, increases from negligible values in solution where dynamin is not polymerized, to rates in the range of 2 to 5 s-1 on optimal membrane templates where dynamin forms spirals (Stowell et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Dynamin was purified from rat brain, which contains mostly the neuron-specific dynamin-1 isoform.
source: Dynamin was purified from rat brain, which contains mostly the neuron-specific dynamin-1 isoform, which has a higher membrane curvature generating activity than dynamin-2, the ubiquitous isoform (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental methods and is supported by a citation.

claim: Dynamin-1 has a higher membrane curvature generating activity than dynamin-2, the ubiquitous isoform.
source: Dynamin was purified from rat brain, which contains mostly the neuron-specific dynamin-1 isoform, which has a higher membrane curvature generating activity than dynamin-2, the ubiquitous isoform (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Conditions exist where dynamin readily self-assembles and undergoes fast GTP hydrolysis and yet does not efficiently promote membrane vesiculation.
source: This second round of analysis is important because conditions exist where dynamin readily self-assembles and undergoes fast GTP hydrolysis and yet does not efficiently promote membrane vesiculation (Neumann and Schmid, 2013; Stowell et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Liposomes containing dipolyunsaturated phospholipids appeared exceptionally malleable as compared to liposomes made of phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsatured acyl chain.
source: Liposomes containing phospholipids with two polyunsaturated acyl chains appeared exceptionally malleable as compared to liposomes made of phospholipids with one saturated and one polyunsatured acyl chain.
evidence: This claim is inferred from electron microscopy observations shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Deformation of spherical liposomes is necessarily accompanied by a diminution of volume of the encapsulated solution.
source: Deformation of spherical liposomes is necessarily accompanied by a diminution of volume of the encapsulated solution.

source: For example, the COPI coat is more efficient at making vesicles from liposomes that have been permeabilized with a pore-forming toxin (Manneville et al., 2008).

claim: Dithionite entry is about 1000 times faster than lipid flip-flop.
source: Previous work established that dithionite entry is about 1000 times faster than lipid flip-flop (Armstrong et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.

source: Therefore, the slow phase in PE-NBD quenching experiments should reflect dithionite permeability.

claim: The tubes were surrounded by a protein spiral with a pitch of ~20 nm characteristic of the endophilin-dynamin complex.
source: The tubes were surrounded by a protein spiral with a pitch of ~20 nm characteristic of the endophilin-dynamin complex (Farsad et al., 2001; Pinot et al., 2014; Sundborger et al., 2011) (Figure 4B and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).

claim: The propensity of membranes to undergo deformation and fission correlates with the unsaturation level of the phospholipid sn2 acyl chain.
source: Thus, the coarse-grained simulations agreed well with the experiments: the propensity of membranes to undergo deformation and fission correlates with the unsaturation level of the phospholipid sn2 acyl chain.

claim: The rough features distinguishing the saturated and the polyunsaturated acyl chains remained after having permutated their position.
source: In all atom simulations, we observed that the rough features distinguishing the saturated and the polyunsaturated acyl chains remained after having permutated their position.
evidence: This claim is supported by all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A.

claim: With natural 18:0-22:6 phospholipids, the sn1 saturated FA showed a peak in the bilayer center whereas the sn2 polyunsaturated FA showed a characteristic dip.
source: In natural phospholipids, the density profile of the sn1 saturated FA showed a peak in the bilayer center whereas the sn2 polyunsaturated FA showed a characteristic dip.
evidence: This claim is supported by all-atom molecular dynamics simulation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3B.

claim: The sn1 saturated FA tail invaded the central region of the bilayer left vacant by the sn2 polyunsaturated FA, which goes up.
source: This shift indicates that the sn1 saturated FA tail invaded the central region of the bilayer left vacant by the sn2 polyunsaturated FA, which goes up (Eldho et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is inferred from simulation data and supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: With swapped 22:6-18:0 phospholipids, the difference in density between saturated and polyunsaturated acyl chains disappeared and the membrane appeared thinner than with natural 18:0-22:6 phospholipids.
source: With swapped 22:6-18:0 phospholipids, this difference in density disappeared and the membrane appeared thinner than with natural 18:0-22:6 phospholipids (Figure 6—figure supplement 3B).

claim: The propensity of the membrane to undergo tubulation and fission increased with the level of phospholipid polyunsaturation (18:1-18:0 < 20:4-18:0 ≈ 22:6-18:0) in coarse-grained simulations of swapped phospholipids.
source: In coarse-grained simulations, the propensity of the membrane to undergo tubulation and fission increased with the level of phospholipid polyunsaturation (18:1-18:0 < 20:4-18:0 ≈ 22:6-18:0), that is the same trend as that observed on classical sn1-saturated-sn2-unsaturated membranes (Figure 6—figure supplement 3C).
